rv.q: It feels as though Richard has invited us into her office (handsomely designed by Shokie Tseumah with props by Tyson Carter) to share her story — one that’s certainly worth listening to.
Black Girl from a White Suburb is a must-see, in my book.
Directed by J. Nicole Brooks, Richard delivers a warm and thoughtful perspective on how growing up as the only Black child in her classes affected her worldview, citing W.E.B.
Everyone can take a message from “Black Girl from a White Suburb” and spend days mulling it over, questioning it, dissecting it, and learning from it.
Richard’s storytelling skills are nicely honed, and she engages the audience beautifully.

cn.t: Critics praise Tania Richard's compelling autobiographical solo show, with her powerful performance and intimate storytelling earning strong reviews. The 65-minute piece resonates as an engaging exploration of identity and Black experience.
